About Event

🚀Make an impact on real world problems in a single weekend!🚀
HSI is back for our third year in a row! Join Hack for Social Impact once again to tackle real-world challenges . We are teaming up with non-profit partners to present you with important and well-scoped challenges, in partnership with UN Convention to Combat Desertification and 4 local nonprofits.
This event is supported by our sponsors: Gemini, Bild.ai , and Wefunder. Developers will receive credits during the hackathon to work on your projects from our sponsors and technology partners.
$5000 cash prizes in total for the winners of projects
This year, we've teamed up with incredible partners to tackle pressing issues in mental health, climate, justice reform, and art & design:

🌎 Climate : Work with the UN to build an interactive game to enable the community to participate in land planning! Block by Block is a Minecraft-based tool for communities to design their own streets, and has run in 55 countries since 2012. However, it is unsuited to UNCCD's work in real-world land planning: Minecraft has endless resources, arbitrary terrain, and no consequence to player actions. Build a game from real satellite and GIS data showing the impact of land use, to engage the community.
🌱 Community Resilience: The East Bay Permaculture Guild brings neighbors together through garden work parties, community gatherings, and local regeneration projects. But welcoming newcomers and promoting events across websites, email lists, and messaging groups falls on a handful of volunteers. Interest fades without follow-up, and repetitive outreach leaves organizers stretched thin. Build simple tools to help the Guild welcome new members, understand how they want to participate, and turn event details into outreach ready for volunteer review. Keep it affordable, easy for volunteers to maintain, and true to the personal connections that make the community worth joining.
🩷 Mental Health : Boundless Freedom Project can reach people inside with mindfulness and mental health practice through in-person sessions and the Edovo tablets. On release that support falls away, during the 30 days that hit hardest. Build something that keeps familiar practice at hand, holds as little personal information as possible, and assumes no smartphone and no dependable internet.
⚖️ Justice Reform : California's corrections department spends under one percent of its budget on rehabilitation. Transformative Programming Works advocates for them across 120 organizations, but so far can only track process data such as who enrolled and how long a class ran. Join disjoint records such as parole and recidivism data into a framework TPW, and nonprofits generally, can use to track impact.

🎨 Art & Design : BRIDGEGOOD's Oakland studio teaches designers to build with their own communities in mind, through conversations about identity, money and conflict that only work in a small room with a facilitator in it. That room seats a few dozen people a year. Find a way the practice can travel to designers who will never sit in it, without thinning into a slide deck.
🏆 Past winners went to present at UN Climate Conference and build startups that get accepted to YC and raise seed funding!🎯 Will your weekend hack be next year's success story?
✨Register your interest and follow us on our LinkedIn for more Partner & Prize announcements ✨
For more information on the event and a recap of last year, visit our website !
✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨
🤝 Who should sign up? Anyone with a passion to build. Whether you are a technical engineer or a non-technical innovator, if you want to team up with smart, driven people to create positive change, you belong here. Bring your unique skills and the energy to make the world a better place to spend the weekend solving real problems together.
Interested in joining the HSI team? Contact us!
Interested in becoming a sponsor? Contact us!
Interested in work working with our partners? Join the list!

Bright Data

Bright Data

San Francisco, CA

Registration

Welcome! To join the event, please register below.
Register

About Event

Join us for the Patch the Conference Hackathon, right before GitHub Universe, where we're looking for builders who can find what's broken about conferences and ship the patch. If something about conferences has ever bugged you, this is your chance to build the fix.
Winners take away iPhone Duos, and there are more cool prizes that we'll announce soon. There's plenty of swag for everyone, plus free OpenAI credits to build with.
Age Requirement: This event is 21+. Valid government-issued photo ID will be checked at the door, no exceptions. Please come prepared with your ID, as entry will not be granted without one.
🗓️ Agenda
9:00 AM: Doors open

9:00 AM to 10:00 AM: Grab breakfast, get set up, start hacking and get familiar with the tools

10:00 AM to 11:00 AM: Workshops and talks from our sponsors to get you up and running

11:00 AM to 2:00 PM: Back to building

2:00 PM: Pizzas arrive, lunch is served

2:00 PM to 6:00 PM: Keep hacking and submit your project

6:00 PM to 7:00 PM: Judging, with teams showcasing their projects on stage

7:00 PM: Winners announced and the iPhone Duos handed over

🛠️ Tools
FalkorDB
FalkorDB is an open-source graph database built for AI agents. Agents are only as good as the context they work with, and a graph gives yours connected data it can reason over, a memory it keeps between sessions, and a clear picture of how things relate.
Here is how you can use it in your project:
Follow connections across data: let your agent answer questions that take more than one hop, with graph queries as its tools.

Remember across sessions: store conversation history and what the agent has learned, so it picks up where it left off.

Share state between agents: give multiple agents one graph to read and write, so handoffs between them work.

Connect people, projects and decisions: bring knowledge from docs, tickets and chats into one graph.

Show the path behind an answer: trace every answer back to the data it came from.

It runs locally with Docker, you query it with Cypher, and it works with Python, Node.js, Java, Rust, Go, PHP and C#.
OpenAI
OpenAI is giving free credits to everyone building at the hackathon, so you can use their models in your project at no cost.
Qodo
Use Qodo in your GitHub repo and it will review your PRs for bugs, logic errors and code quality issues before you merge.
Come solo or form a team of up to 4 people. If you win and don't want the phone, you can take the cash prize instead.

Kane CLI Hack Day, supported by OpenAI

TestMu AI

Register to See Address
San Francisco, CA

Registration

Registration Closed

This event is not currently taking registrations. You may contact the host or subscribe to receive updates.

About Event

Build it with OpenAI. Validate with Kane.
Kane CLI Hack Day SF, Supported by OpenAI.
Build it with an agent. Verify it with Kane.
Your agent can write an app in minutes. On October 24 you find out if that app actually works.
We're taking over a room in San Francisco for a full day of building with AI coding agents, with support from OpenAI. Kane CLI runs on OpenAI models under the hood, so for one Saturday the models that help write your code are also the ones checking it.
$30,000+ in prizes and credits
Saturday, October 24 · San Francisco · Hosted by TestMu AI, supported by OpenAI.
Seats are limited and every registration is reviewed. Apply early.
The Challenge
Build a working app with any AI coding agent. Use Kane CLI to prove it works. Ship by 6 PM.
That's all there is to it. Build a tool, a dashboard, a game, an internal utility, a strange experiment, or the side project that's been sitting in your notes app since spring. Just follow two rules:
Kane CLI has to verify your app. At minimum, run it at demo time. The teams that win will go further and put Kane inside the agent: a hook that runs Kane on every save, an agent that reads Kane's NDJSON output and keeps fixing until the flows pass, or a spec that compiles straight into Kane flows.

Your app has to run, ship and survive a live demo. Judges want to see it working in front of them.

Come solo or bring a team of up to four. Bring your laptop and your stack. We'll cover food, coffee, credits and help on the floor.
Pick your track
Web App: The fastest route from idea to verified. Kane CLI works on web apps right out of the box.

Mobile App: Build for iOS or Android and watch Kane test it on real devices through TestMu AI's device cloud.

Wildcard: Anything goes, as long as it ships and Kane can verify it.

Special Prize, Most Innovative Use of Kane CLI: For the team that does something with Kane that we didn't see coming.

The Prizes
🥇 1st Place: Apple Vision Pro + $3,000 in OpenAI credits

🥈 2nd Place: Apple Mac mini + $2,000 in OpenAI credits

🥉 3rd Place: Apple iPad + $1,000 in OpenAI credits

Every winning team also gets:
A 1:1 with the TestMu AI founders

Design partner status, with a say in the Kane CLI roadmap

A featured post on the TestMu blog

A spot on the Kane CLI showcase

A push across TestMu and dev.to channels

Every builder walks away with
$250 in OpenAI credits

3 months of KaneAI Pro (worth $270)

A full day of food, swag, and a room full of people shipping with agents

Before you arrive
Bring the agent you already use. CLI agents, IDE agents, chat agents, MCP setups or one you built yourself all work. Install it and sign in before you get here.

Install Kane CLI and run one flow. Run npm install -g @testmuai/kane-cli and try an example from the docs. A whole room running fresh npm installs at 10:05 AM costs everyone the first hour. Your confirmation email includes a cheat sheet.

Set up your OpenAI API account. Your confirmation email will explain how to claim your $250 in credits.

FAQs
Do I have to build with OpenAI? Participants receive $250 in OpenAI API credits.
Which AI agent should I use? Whichever one you already build with. Terminal agents, IDE agents, browser agents, custom agents, MCP servers and multi-agent setups all count. Kane CLI is the one required layer, and everything above it is your call.
Which other AI tools can I use? Anything that helps you ship. There's no approved-tools list, so bring your own models, frameworks and scaffolding.
Do I need a paid Kane CLI plan? No. Every builder gets 3 months of KaneAI Pro, starting on event day.
Can I bring a project I've already started? Yes, but the Kane CLI integration has to happen on the day. At demo time, show what existed at 10 AM and what you built after that. Judges will weight the new work.
Can I work solo? Absolutely. Solo builders are welcome, and so are teams of up to four.
Do I need to know Playwright or Selenium? No. Kane CLI works in plain English: describe the flow and Kane runs it. If you know Playwright, the built-in export is a nice bonus for your writeup.
What if my project breaks during demos? Test hard before 5 PM, because submissions lock at the deadline and you can't push fixes during demos. If your app depends on a third-party service, keep a recorded run or a backup deploy ready so judges still see what you built.

Register

About Event

🎟️ REGISTER FIRST (both are required)
1️⃣ AWS registration, needed to enter the building https://events.builder.aws.com/EARgN9
2️⃣ Join the Discord Join Discord Server
Space is limited.
⚠️ ENTRY REQUIREMENTS
18+ only

Valid government-issued physical photo ID at check-in. Digital IDs will not be accepted.

No scooters or bikes inside any Amazon building. No on-site parking.

The Universal Celebration Hackathon is a celebration of creativity, entrepreneurship, and the next generation of AI-powered companies. Bring your ideas, experiment with new possibilities, and turn your vision into something real.
This hackathon is about more than building prototypes, chatbots, or collections of AI agents. It’s about imagining what happens when AI agents become a team of digital people who can collaborate, communicate, make decisions, and perform real-world work together.
The Challenge
Build an AI-powered company, business, or organization run by a team of AI agents.
Your challenge is to create an AI-native business that demonstrates how multiple specialized agents can work together in a practical, real-world use case.
Think beyond a conventional startup team. Your agents could run a restaurant, manage a retail shop, operate a travel agency, coordinate social services, produce a film, or build an entirely new kind of business.
Each agent should have a distinct role, responsibility, personality, and character. Give them avatars and voices, and demonstrate how they interact with one another, exchange information, delegate tasks, make decisions, and work toward a shared goal.
The agents should do more than talk. They should use tools, conduct research, automate workflows, execute tasks, manage business operations, and deliver tangible outcomes.
The key question is:
What happens when you give a team of AI agents a real-world mission, distinct identities, and the tools to get the job done?
What to Build
Build a working prototype of a real-world operation powered by a team of collaborating AI agents.
Your project should:
Solve a real problem: Identify a practical need, business opportunity, or community challenge.

Create at least five AI agents: Give each agent a distinct role, responsibility, character, avatar, and voice.

Demonstrate real interactions: Show agents communicating, sharing context, coordinating responsibilities, and making decisions together.

Operate in a real-world use case: Demonstrate your agents performing actual business or organizational tasks, rather than simply discussing what they could do.

Use tools and automation: Enable agents to conduct browser-based and deep research, execute code in a sandbox, and automate workflows.

Build with reliability and security: Include code review, code-quality checks, and security vulnerability detection and remediation as part of your development workflow.

Show business value: Explain how your AI-powered company delivers value, serves customers or communities, and could grow over time.

Your agents might include a CEO, product manager, engineer, marketer, salesperson, finance specialist, or customer-support representative. Alternatively, they could be a chef, restaurant manager, inventory coordinator, and customer-service team working together to run a restaurant.
The roles should make sense for the real-world operation you choose.
Choose one or multiple tracks and build your company within them.
Tracks
Climate, Sustainability & Impact
Build AI solutions for a healthier planet and stronger communities.
Examples: climate, sustainability, agriculture, disaster response, smart cities, social impact.
Health, Wellness & Care
Build AI solutions that improve health, wellbeing, and quality of life.
Examples: healthcare, fitness, nutrition, mental wellness, elder care.
Education, Learning & Research
Build AI solutions that make learning, education, and research better.
Examples: tutoring, personalized learning, professional training, research, career development.
Business, Growth & Productivity
Build AI solutions that help businesses work smarter, grow faster, and operate better.
Examples: sales, marketing, CRM, analytics, productivity, automation, business operations.
Media, Entertainment & Creators
Build AI solutions for creativity, entertainment, and digital experiences.
Examples: film, music, gaming, content creation, creator tools, social media.
Commerce, Retail & Consumer
Build AI solutions that transform how people shop and how businesses sell.
Examples: e-commerce, marketplaces, retail, logistics, inventory, personalized shopping.
Build the Future
Don't just build multiple AI agents. Give them characters, a mission, a workplace, and the tools to work together. Show us what they can accomplish as a team.
Sponsors & Tools
Masky.AI

Masky.ai gives agents a face, voice, and brain. At the hackathon we'll give credits to clone yourself or bring your own characters to life.

Then bring your agents into Maskord.com - discord for humans and agents. Connect agents built with your favorite coding harnesses and let your friends, teammates, and their agents all talk and work together in the same channels.

Aly will talk briefly about mental wellness and Living Book where she turned herself and her book into an interactive voice/avatar agent that creates audio and talks with fans online identifying social media posts and giving her notifications when people post content related to her focus.

$800 in prizes awarded to teams that keep human communities safe as we bring this new intelligence online at scale. Agents should participate in human communities, not replace them. Masky is the place where the agent workforce becomes social. See more on our blog https://masky.ai/blog/2026-10-14-ai-workforce-hackathon/
RocketRide:
RocketRide is an open-source, developer-native AI meta-harness. Build, debug, and deploy production AI workflows right inside your IDE. And with RocketRide Cloud , teams can offload the complexity of AI infrastructure and focus on building solutions, with cost-efficient execution through our proprietary model server, shared pipelines for collaboration, higher performance, and seamless scalability.
🎁 Free credits: We're giving away free credits for RocketRide Cloud, 100% off your first purchase with a promo code. Join the Discord to grab yours.

Need help? Just ask our bot in #support (Discord) whether it’s about your project or the tools.

Join top AI engineers, founders, and builders at the AWS Builder Loft in San Francisco for a full day of building production-ready AI agents powered by live web data.

Challenge: Invisible Interfaces
The best interface is sometimes no interface at all. This edition explores products that work through voice, motion, sensors, live data, autonomous agents, and other natural interactions.
Build technology that helps people or systems sense, decide, and act without relying on a traditional app or screen.
1. Dispatch
Use live data such as ship traffic, flight data, fleet GPS, sensors, or border wait times to move physical things where they need to go.
Build for logistics, transportation, ports, emergency response, or defense.
2. No App
Build for people who will never open an app, including seniors, drivers, nurses, warehouse workers, and field crews.
Use voice, phone calls, glasses, vibration, or another invisible interface. If users have to look at a screen, it does not count.
3. Unsupervised
Build agents that run for hours without constant supervision.
Your system should know when it is stuck, overspending, looping, or when it needs to stop.
4. AI-Powered Consumer Products for 1 Billion People
Build an AI-powered consumer product that reaches people through natural, ambient, or invisible interactions.
Rethink how people discover, use, and benefit from technology beyond traditional apps and screens. The strongest ideas will address a clear everyday need and have the potential to serve people at global scale.

Welcome! To join the event, please register below.
Request to Join

About Event

Build It. Test It. Prove It.
Free 3-day Sprint for pre-seed founders. October 21 to 23, SAP Labs, Palo Alto.
Judges from Stanford, Nvidia, Meta, and Microsoft AI spend three days watching how your team actually works, then question you on it. You leave with a clearer next move and a scored record of how you operate, built for investor conversations.
Past teams have gone on to raise from 500 Global and Blitzscaling Ventures and join Berkeley SkyDeck and Confluent's accelerator.
20 team spots. Applications close Oct 14
Judges
Mohammad Rasouli Phd., Researcher, AI for Private Markets, Stanford
Sajal Garg, Principal Soft Eng, Microsoft AI
Abhinav Balasubramanian, AI Lead, Nvidia
Tharun Tej Tammineni, AI Lead, Meta
What this is
Judges who lead AI at Nvidia, Meta, Microsoft AI, and Stanford spend three days watching how your team works, then question you on it. They'll push on your build, your technical claims, and how your team decides. Better here than in a pitch meeting.
You leave with a clearer next move and a scored record of how you operate. Evidence you can bring to investors, not a pitch deck you rehearsed.
Two tracks
Discovery Track. Pre-market, no customer contact yet. For founders seriously exploring a startup, including people inside companies weighing the leap.
Pre-Seed Track. In-market, already talking to customers. Ship something real, show what changed, pressure-test your next move.
What you get
No cash. No trophy. Something more useful.
Teams that clear the Sprint's scoring bar earn the Street Test : 30 days back in the real world, building with no event deadline and no audience, just you and the market. It's a bar, not a ranking. Every team that clears it gets in.
Teams that finish the Street Test receive a Proving Ground report card , a scored record of how you operated across both stages. It covers three things: whether customers are pulling (Pull), whether progress held up after the event (Momentum), and whether this team fits this problem (Founder Fit). It's yours - bring it to investors, accelerators, or a cofounder you're recruiting.
A hackathon ends when the event does. This doesn't.
Schedule
Wednesday, Oct 21: 9am to 8pm. Kickoff, building begins.
Thursday, Oct 22: 9am to 8pm. Full build day.
Friday, Oct 23: 9am to 4pm. Finals, live defense, deliberation, awards.
Who should apply
Pre-seed founders with live customer conversations.
Builders, product leaders, designers, and operators ready to test an idea for real.
University students: the commitment is all three days, Wednesday to Friday, 9am to close. Limited undergrad spots.

About Event

Pick a subscription and build its replacement.
That software subscription you keep complaining about? You’ve got one day to build something better.
Join us at the Seldon Speakeasy in SoMa . Pick a paid product, rethink a key workflow and build an alternative someone would actually switch to.
🛠️ Pick your target. A dev tool, a design tool or a CRM - it's your call. Choose something you can meaningfully reinvent in a day. Bring a team or find your people when you arrive.

Build with anything. Test with Wren. Use your favourite stack and coding tools. Put Wren, Seldon’s QA agent , to work while you build: test real journeys through your app, fix what breaks and run it again. We’ll provide access, credits and hands-on help.

The demo has a twist. Someone from the Seldon team runs the demo. Can they do what your product promises? You’ll get to explain your idea, then let them try it.

🏆 Three ways to win. Prizes for best overall product , most original reinvention and people’s choice . Originality, usefulness and whether it actually works all count. Up to $5k in prizes.

🍸 Finish at the bar. Demos, prizes and drinks behind the red velvet curtains. Meet the Seldon team and the people you’ve spent the day building alongside.

To qualify for prizes: submit a working product and Wren test results for at least two core workflows, rerun against your final build.
Bring a laptop and a subscription you’d like to stop paying for.

Registration

Approval Required

Welcome! To join the event, please register below.
Request to Join

About Event

Build physical AI applications with real robot arms.

About the Event
Viam and MongoDB are excited to host a two-day, hands-on hackathon for curious, ambitious builders who want to go deep on physical AI. You'll get a real robot arm and support from Viam experts throughout.
No prior robotics experience is required, just an interest in physical AI and some software experience.
Space is limited! Apply through this page. Applicants will be accepted on a rolling basis.

What You'll Build
Working in a team of 2-3, you'll build an end-to-end robotics application using Viam and a real robot arm.

Each team will have access to:
UFactory xArm or Universal Robots arm with a two-finger gripper attachment (feel free to also bring your own SO-101)

Linux compute machine

RealSense D435 or Orbbec Astra 2 camera (fixed to arm)

Webcams

A free Viam account

A MongoDB Atlas cluster for storing and querying your robot's data: sensor readings, grasp attempts, run logs and embeddings

We’ll provide a variety of objects for your robot to manipulate. You are encouraged to bring anything required for the project you have in mind.
Please bring your own laptop.
In your application, please summarize what project you have in mind.
Ideas from past events: training a VLA, playing chess, mixing a cocktail, quality inspection, drawing a picture, puzzle insertion, manipulating a robot arm using computer vision and hand gestures.
Build with MongoDB Atlas
Robots produce a lot of data, and the best teams use it.
Every team gets MongoDB Atlas to give their robot a memory. Some ideas:
Log every attempt (poses, gripper force, camera metadata, success or failure) and query it to tune your approach between runs

Use Atlas Vector Search to match what the camera sees against known objects, which helps with the recycling sort or open-track ideas

Store task plans, scene descriptions or past outcomes so an LLM-driven robot can retrieve context before it acts

Build a live dashboard of your benchmark runs

Using Atlas isn't required, but strong, creative uses of it will stand out to the judges.
Prizes
We'll award prizes to a total of three teams. Each member of a winning team will take home SO-101 pre-assembled robot kits, including: a leader arm, a follower arm, and a camera + Viam credits.
Gold: SO-101 arm + $5,000 in MongoDB Atlas credits and $5,000 in Viam credits

Silver: SO-101 arm + $2,500 in MongoDB Atlas credits and $2,500 in Viam credits

Bronze: SO-101 arm + $1,000 in MongoDB Atlas credits and $1,000 in Viam credits

Please bring your own laptop. We recommend taking our free online course Viam 101 (est time: 45-90mins) ahead of time. Even if you only go through the first lessons, it will help you get the hang of things quickly.
Schedule
Thursday, October 29
9:00 AM: Check-in and breakfast
9:30 AM: Kickoff: Welcome & crash course on building with Viam and MongoDB
10:00 AM: Teams and hardware
10:30 AM: Hacking begins
1:00 PM: Lunch
6:00 PM: Dinner
9:00 PM: Hard close: Robots power down, doors close (no overnight hacking)
Friday, October 30
9:00 AM: Doors open, breakfast
9:30 AM: Hacking resumes
12:30 PM: Lunch
3:30 PM: Demos and drinks
5:00 PM: Awards
6:00 PM: Event concludes
What Skills You Need
No robotics experience required, but you should be comfortable with:
Coding: Python, Go, TypeScript/JavaScript, or C++

Linux: Using SSH and running basic terminal commands

JSON: Reading and editing configuration files

Git: Basic workflows so your team can build together

Bonus: knowing how to plug in a pre-trained vision model (like YOLO or OpenCV) to help the robot see and identify objects (not required)

Bonus: Some familiarity with MongoDB or document databases (not required, and mentors can help you get started)

Before the Event
We recommend taking our free online course Viam 101 (est time: 45-90mins) ahead of time. Even the first few lessons will help you get the hang of things quickly.
How to Join
Space is limited! Apply through this page. Applicants will be accepted on a rolling basis.
We’ll select a curated group of ambitious software developers and send official confirmations to accepted participants. Attendees must be approved in advance to participate.
Presented By
Viam : The robotics software platform we’ll use to configure, control, and deploy models to your robot. Viam makes it easy to get a robot up and running quickly.
MongoDB : The developer data platform for storing, searching and analyzing your robot's data, including vector search for AI-powered retrieval.

The Universal Celebration Hackathon is a celebration of creativity, entrepreneurship, and the next generation of AI-powered companies. Bring your ideas, experiment with new possibilities, and turn your vision into something real.
This hackathon is about more than building prototypes, chatbots, or collections of AI agents. It’s about imagining what happens when AI agents become a team of digital people who can collaborate, communicate, make decisions, and perform real-world work together.
The Challenge
Build an AI-powered company, business, or organization run by a team of AI agents.
Your challenge is to create an AI-native business that demonstrates how multiple specialized agents can work together in a practical, real-world use case.
Think beyond a conventional startup team. Your agents could run a restaurant, manage a retail shop, operate a travel agency, coordinate social services, produce a film, or build an entirely new kind of business.
Each agent should have a distinct role, responsibility, personality, and character. Give them avatars and voices, and demonstrate how they interact with one another, exchange information, delegate tasks, make decisions, and work toward a shared goal.
The agents should do more than talk. They should use tools, conduct research, automate workflows, execute tasks, manage business operations, and deliver tangible outcomes.
The key question is:
What happens when you give a team of AI agents a real-world mission, distinct identities, and the tools to get the job done?
What to Build
Build a working prototype of a real-world operation powered by a team of collaborating AI agents.
Your project should:
Solve a real problem: Identify a practical need, business opportunity, or community challenge.

Create at least five AI agents: Give each agent a distinct role, responsibility, character, avatar, and voice.

Demonstrate real interactions: Show agents communicating, sharing context, coordinating responsibilities, and making decisions together.

Operate in a real-world use case: Demonstrate your agents performing actual business or organizational tasks, rather than simply discussing what they could do.

Use tools and automation: Enable agents to conduct browser-based and deep research, execute code in a sandbox, and automate workflows.

Build with reliability and security: Include code review, code-quality checks, and security vulnerability detection and remediation as part of your development workflow.

Show business value: Explain how your AI-powered company delivers value, serves customers or communities, and could grow over time.

Your agents might include a CEO, product manager, engineer, marketer, salesperson, finance specialist, or customer-support representative. Alternatively, they could be a chef, restaurant manager, inventory coordinator, and customer-service team working together to run a restaurant.
The roles should make sense for the real-world operation you choose.
Choose one or multiple tracks and build your company within them.
Tracks
Climate, Sustainability & Impact
Build AI solutions for a healthier planet and stronger communities.
Examples: climate, sustainability, agriculture, disaster response, smart cities, social impact.
Health, Wellness & Care
Build AI solutions that improve health, wellbeing, and quality of life.
Examples: healthcare, fitness, nutrition, mental wellness, elder care.
Education, Learning & Research
Build AI solutions that make learning, education, and research better.
Examples: tutoring, personalized learning, professional training, research, career development.
Business, Growth & Productivity
Build AI solutions that help businesses work smarter, grow faster, and operate better.
Examples: sales, marketing, CRM, analytics, productivity, automation, business operations.
Media, Entertainment & Creators
Build AI solutions for creativity, entertainment, and digital experiences.
Examples: film, music, gaming, content creation, creator tools, social media.
Commerce, Retail & Consumer
Build AI solutions that transform how people shop and how businesses sell.
Examples: e-commerce, marketplaces, retail, logistics, inventory, personalized shopping.
Build the Future
Don't just build multiple AI agents. Give them characters, a mission, a workplace, and the tools to work together. Show us what they can accomplish as a team.

SEO/GEO × Organic Content × AI-Native Growth

Weijia — Founder & CEO, LingCode
Developer Growth × Product-Led Growth × Community
Built content reaching millions, grew a coding education platform from 0 → 10,000+ students , and took LingCode from launch to 1,000+ users in its first month . Learn how technical founders can turn product, content, and community into an organic growth engine.
Ben Weinmann — Growth @ Magnific

UGC × AI Content × Organic Growth Growth operator specializing in organic distribution, UGC programs, AI-powered content, and short-form growth. Ben will share how to generate millions of views at a low cost, why audience trust matters more than follower count alone when driving conversions, and the challenges of attributing revenue to content across multiple marketing channels.
Talk: From Views to Conversion: What Actually Works in UGC & AI Content
More founders & GTM operators to be announced.

Most hackathons ask you to build another demo.
Here, you'll work on a real product with real users and a real GTM problem — then use AI, code, content, outbound, SEO/GEO, automation, communities, or whatever else you can invent to move the numbers.
💻 AI Developer Tools — LingCode
How do you win developers when every week brings another AI coding tool?
Grow an AI-native IDE through developer communities, technical content, product-led loops, GEO, creators, or your own growth automation.
Learn: developer GTM, PLG, community growth, and how technical products earn adoption.
🎾 Consumer Community — Tennistry
3,500+ users. 1,500+ real tennis matches. How do you create the next 1,000?
Tennistry connects tennis players in real life. Test local acquisition, referrals, ambassadors, events, creators, and ways to prove which users you actually brought in.
Learn: consumer growth, network effects, referral loops, local/community GTM, and attribution.
🇺🇸 High-Trust Services — TurboNIW
How do you acquire customers when the decision is expensive, complex, and built on trust?
TurboNIW helps STEM researchers and professionals prepare for the EB-2 NIW process through structured educational materials and guidance. Unlike a casual app download, customers may spend $1,000+ and are making a high-stakes career decision—making trust and intent central to acquisition. TurboNIW
Learn: high-intent SEO/GEO, trust-based funnels, educational content, lead qualification, and customer acquisition for high-consideration services.
💳 Consumer FinTech — MaxWorth
30,000 users already. What becomes the next scalable growth channel?

Learn: consumer FinTech GTM, lifecycle growth, referral mechanics, content distribution, and scaling beyond early adopters.
🎬 Generative AI × Entertainment — SceneMixer.com
A new AI creative product is starting from zero. Where do the first 100 real users come from?
SceneMixer is an AI short-drama generation platform. Find the creators and communities most likely to care, then experiment with UGC, viral formats, creator seeding, social distribution, and product-led sharing.
Learn: 0→1 launches, creator GTM, UGC, viral loops, and consumer AI distribution.

💹 Financial AI — Winus
How do you grow a financial AI product in a market where trust, accuracy, and professional credibility matter as much as product experience?
Winus is a financial AI platform built for research and decision-making, combining financial chat, deep research, fact-checking, agents, and skills for finance professionals. Test ways to reach and convert relevant users through finance communities, professional content, SEO/GEO, partnerships, referrals, or other measurable GTM experiments.
Learn: financial AI GTM, trust-driven acquisition, professional-user growth, content distribution, and conversion in high-intent markets.

About Event

🛑 Learning was never text-only. Kids read out loud, scribble on worksheets, point at diagrams, and think with their hands. Now AI can hear, see, and watch too.
SVAI Arrival Guide .pdf
Multi-Modal AI for Education
A text box only catches what a student types. A great teacher notices much more: the pause before a hard word, the crossed-out step in a math problem, the moment a class goes quiet. Multi-modal AI can finally pick up those signals. Voice, handwriting, images, and video can all become part of how we teach.
The hard part isn't the demo. It's building tools that teachers and families actually trust, and showing that students really learned more. That takes clear learning outcomes, not just a clever model.
Join Beta Fund and co-host Epic at Snowflake's Silicon Valley AI Hub in Menlo Park for a full day of building multi-modal learning tools. The day includes a panel with voices from Epic , Khan Academy , and Dex on where AI education is headed, plus demos in front of the room.
Build tutors that listen. Build tools that see the work. Build learning you can measure.
⚠️ Approval required. About 120 builders. You need an approved registration to get in: no walk-ins, no +1s. Bring your laptop.

🎙️ Track 1 · Voice & Audio Tutors
Tutors that listen as well as talk. Hear a student read or think out loud, catch exactly where they get stuck, and respond like a patient coach.
Ideas: a read-aloud fluency coach that hears which words a kid stumbles on · a think-aloud math tutor that spots the misconception in a spoken explanation · a speaking partner for language learners · voice-first learning for students with dyslexia or low vision
✍️ Track 2 · Vision, Handwriting & Documents
Learning happens on paper. Build AI that reads handwritten work, worksheets, diagrams, and textbook pages, and gives feedback on the steps, not just the final answer.
Ideas: snap a photo of handwritten math and get step-by-step feedback · grade a stack of scanned worksheets and group the common mistakes · turn a picture-book or textbook page into an interactive lesson · understand a student's science diagram or lab sketch
🎥 Track 3 · Video & Classroom Understanding
Video holds a lot of what happens in teaching and learning. Turn lectures, demonstrations, and classroom moments into feedback for students and teachers.
Ideas: turn a lecture video into chapters, a study guide, and a quiz · give teachers feedback on talk time and questioning from a classroom recording · watch a student's experiment or presentation and coach them on it · a video explainer that adapts to what the learner already knows
📡 Track 4 · Real-Time Multi-Modal Tutors & Agents
Tutors that work live, like sitting next to a great teacher. Combine live video, voice, and screen or camera input so the AI sees what the student is doing and helps in the moment.
Ideas: a tutor on a live video call that watches a student work a problem and nudges at the right time · a screen-aware coding or homework coach · a phone-camera lab assistant for hands-on science · an AR or camera guide that teaches by pointing at real objects
📖 Track 5 · Multi-Modal Storytelling
Stories are how kids learn to read, imagine, and remember. Build AI that blends voice, images, and video into stories that teach, react to the reader, and let kids create their own.
Ideas: turn a child's drawing and voice recording into an illustrated, narrated story · an interactive read-along that reacts to how the reader is doing · turn a history or science lesson into a narrated illustrated or video story · kids co-creating a story by voice, with images generated as they talk · multilingual narration that reads the same story in a child's home language
📊 Track 6 · Multi-Modal Learning Assessment
Build quick, fair, automated ways to understand where a learner is, using voice, handwriting, and interaction instead of long one-on-one tests.
Ideas: a reading-fluency screener that listens to a child read aloud · early dyslexia signals from speech and spelling · a math-fluency check from handwritten work · teacher-ready reports that turn results into next steps
🃏 Wildcard (Open Category)
Any multi-modal idea that doesn't fit the tracks above. If it solves a real problem in learning and shows a measurable learning outcome, build it.

"The way to get startup ideas is not to try to think of startup ideas. It's to look for problems, preferably problems you have yourself." Paul Graham

Most people who want to build something sit in a room and brainstorm ideas. That is the wrong starting point.

The right starting point is a real problem. That is the ITCH worth scratching.

If you do not have that problem yourself, come find it here. ITCH is a panel discussion with business owners or industry experts in the SF community. We dig into what is actually hard in their business right now. Together, we find the ITCH.

You leave with a list of real problems you can actually work on. And some of the panelists might let you pilot your solution with them directly.You can find ways to leverage AI for these problems.

Registration

Welcome! To join the event, please register below.
Register

About Event

Build a Sovereign AI Model Factory: an ML Engineer Agent that evaluates, fine-tunes, deploys, and improves open models using Union on your cloud.
The best AI teams aren't renting every capability from an external API, they're building systems they own and control. In this hands-on session at the AWS Loft, we'll build exactly that.
We'll start with a walkthrough where we build a LangGraph-powered agent that evaluates open models in parallel, fine-tunes promising candidates, deploys the winner, and retrains automatically when performance drops. Think of it as the first brick in your own model factory : a repeatable system for evaluating, improving, and deploying models you control, not a black box you call and hope for the best.
Along the way, you'll see how Union.ai gives your workflows a durable runtime with infrastructure as context, so agents adapt infra resources, recover from failures, and keep moving without re-running completed work. And because it all runs in your own AWS account , you own the full stack end to end: your models, your data, your infrastructure, your IP.
Then we switch into hack night mode : keep building on the example, bring your own models or datasets, experiment with evals and fine-tuning, extend open models to different parts of your agent, or start something new around the same ideas.
For teams thinking about sovereign AI , this is a practical starting point for owning more of your stack, the weights, the training loop, the evals, and the infrastructure it runs on, all on AWS.
Bring a laptop. Leave with a factory.

All guests must be 18+ and present a valid government-issued physical photo ID at check-in (digital IDs are not accepted). Scooters and bikes are not permitted in any Amazon building, and there is no on-site parking.

About Event

Physical AI is moving into the real world as we always imagined.
Machines can now handle objects with real dexterity, feel what they touch, coordinate their whole body, and adapt on the fly.
The question is how far we can push it. Not just better robots, but any system that can perceive, reason, and act reliably in the physical world.
What you’re building for
Perception

Spatial intelligence + world models

Movement + dexterity

Autonomy

Human-machine interaction

What to Expect
🧠 Support from Google DeepMind + partners

🛠️ Tools for robotics, simulation, perception + embodied AI

⚡ Build, test + iterate

🎤 Final demos + judging

Your Judges
Vineeth Kalluru - Gen AI Solutions Architect @ Nvidia
Who should deploy?
Robotics engineers, ML/AI engineers, researchers, hardware builders, autonomous systems engineers, technical founders, and developers exploring Physical AI.
Bring a team of 2-4. Solo? Find teammates in our Discord before kickoff.

Registration

Event Full
If you’d like, you can join the waitlist.

Please click on the button below to join the waitlist. You will be notified if additional spots become available.
Join Waitlist

About Event

This hack, we're headed back to Studio 45 for a hardware focused hack and build weekend in partnership with Claude Community and other partners.
We're also hosting a warm up build day Oct 17 if you want to join early to make a team and get started on a project.
No pre-reqs. All scientists, software, and hardware engineers welcome.
We welcome all skill levels and can support 50 builders.

Teams will be formed on the spot, and will work through custom automation challenges with sample prep, instrument integration, as well as an open track

⭐️ You must be able to stay through demo on Sunday to participate in the hack . Everyone joining will be expected to demo something by end of the weekend.

Track A: Sample Prep with BioKEA
BioKEA does DNA barcoding, environmental DNA, and long-read genomics from soil, water, or specimen to a verifiable, FAIR-compliant published claim.
They work with open sourced hardware and need help making the sample prep process more robust with a robotic sieving process.
There will also be chances to iterate on other parts of the workcell.
Track B: TBA
We're working with a few different instrument partners and will announce more soon.
Track C: Open build
We'll have extra robotic arms, cameras, and 3d printers for you to build on dexterity challenges or your own problem space.
You can also bring your own hardware.
Saturday agenda
9:30a Check in + breakfast

10:00a Kickoff

11:00a Finalize teams

12:00p Hack + build #1

6:00p Dinner + Round table talks

7:00p Hack + build #2

12:00a Robots go to sleep.

Sunday agenda
8a Doors Open

230p Final submission

330p-430p Live demos showcase

430-530p Demos + Pitching

🤖 ** Register for final demos **
Thank you to our sponsors for helping make it happen!
Host partner
Studio 45 - informal spaces SF is a physical space for entrepreneurs and teams building hardware in SF. Located in Mission/Bernal Area, the studio gathers the community, resources, space, and tools needed to build a business making physical products.

Technical track partners
BioKEA is a 5,000+ sq ft Berkeley wet-lab. The lab does DNA barcoding, environmental DNA, and long-read genomics from soil, water, or specimen to a verifiable, FAIR-compliant published claim. Built for the commons.

Community partners
Claude Community is where builders, educators, and researchers meet to share what they're making with Claude and push each other to build what's next.

Bay area lab automators is a community of scientists, engineers, and tinkerers working at the intersection of hardware, software, and lab innovation.

SF Hardware Meetup , community of 10,000+ hardware professionals meeting monthly to building meaningful connections

Worldwide Studios hosts fellowships and build experiences for scientists to get hands on with the latest in AI, robotics, and hardware. CA 501c3 non-profit.

If you want to help sponsor this event or volunteer send us a note at michael (at) raspuzzi (dot) com

About Event

What if your company had a shared brain that could understand its documents, tools, processes, people, and institutional knowledge—and make that knowledge available to employees and AI agents?
In this afernoon hands-on hackathon, participants will build a working Company Brain: an AI-powered knowledge system that connects information from sources such as documentation, meeting notes, FAQs, policies, product information, support content, and internal tools.
TechEquity Ai invites you to an afternoon of applied AI learning and hands-on building at Snowflake's Silicon Valley AI Hub (SVAI) in Menlo Park, CA.
This session is part of the TechEquity Ai Monthly Forum Series , combining strategic insights and real-world use cases from industry leaders, alongside technical workshops and live demonstrations.

About Event

On-Device AI Hackathon: Cleared for Takeoff ✈️
What if you could build an AI application that works, even when the Wi-Fi doesn't?
Your flight is preparing for takeoff. Once the cabin doors close, your connection to the cloud disappears. Before switching to airplane mode, you have one mission: build an AI project that runs entirely on-device.
In this hands-on hackathon from Qualcomm × Liquid AI , you'll team up with a flight crew of up to four people to build with Liquid Foundation Models (LFMs) and Qualcomm iQ9s. At the end of the night, we'll turn off the Wi-Fi and put every project to the test.
Will your project survive offline?
Why on-device AI?
Unlike traditional AI applications that depend on cloud servers, on-device AI runs models directly on the user's hardware. That means your product can benefit from:
Low latency ⚡

Greater user privacy 🔒

No server inference costs 💸

Offline functionality 📴

Who this is for
👨‍💻 Developers who want to ship AI features without an inference bill

🤖 ML and AI engineers curious about deploying models beyond the cloud

⚙️ Edge, embedded, and robotics engineers building against real hardware constraints

🚀 Founders and product managers evaluating on-device versus cloud AI

🎓 Students and self-taught builders who want to leave having built something real

You don't need previous on-device development experience. If you can run a script, you can join the flight.
Teams may have up to four people . You can arrive with a team or meet your crew at the event.

Request to Join

About Event

What’s one go-to-market task you’d happily hand off to AI? Researching accounts, preparing for customer meetings, or pulling together the same report again?
Join us for a beginner-friendly afternoon of learning and building with PromptQL . This hackathon is for sales and marketing teams, revenue operations professionals, and startup founders who want to try AI on work they actually do.
👀 See how we use PromptQL for GTM
To start, Adam Malone , VP, Forward Deployed Engineering at PromptQL, will show us how he uses PromptQL in his team’s work.
He’ll walk through a connected GTM workflow:
Find the right people using research and the contacts you already know.

Map the account with an org chart and context on key stakeholders.

Prepare for the meeting with a custom demo tailored to the people and their business.

Turn the call into a follow-up email, a personalized video, and clear next steps.

Bring that context back into your CRM, with proposed updates and actions for your team to review.

We’ll also explore how that context can help with event invitations and ideas for marketing content. Bring your questions and pick up a few ideas for your own team.
🛠️ Then, it’s your turn to tinker
We’ll help you get set up, then give you time to experiment and build GTM bots and apps. Come with an idea, a problem you’d like to solve, or just some curiosity.
We encourage you to bring a teammate so you can experience multiplayer AI on work you share. It’s not required, and you’re welcome to come on your own.
You don’t need to be a developer or have previous hackathon experience. We’ll provide participants with PromptQL credits to build with during the hackathon, plus snacks and drinks 🍿🥤.
At the end, anyone who wants to can share what they’ve made, followed by audience voting and a wrap-up.

SVCE also offers innovative local programs and education to help customers save money, improve the health of the region, and achieve aggressive carbon-reduction goals by upgrading to all-electric equipment.

The legal industry touches nearly everyone and has changed less than almost any other sector in the last few decades — this weekend is about building the tools that could finally change that, from AI that helps a tenant fight an eviction to software that lets a small business draft a contract without a $400-an-hour phone call.
Around 100 participants will pitch ideas, form teams around the strongest ones, and spend the weekend building toward a final pitch to a panel of judges. Mentors and coaches work alongside teams throughout, helping them get out of the building to validate ideas with real users, sharpen product direction, and prepare a polished final pitch.
Julian Bryant , Lead Organizer of Techstars Startup Weekend San Diego and an attorney/software developer himself, has facilitated roughly 40 Startup Weekends and brings a track record of real companies launched from the format — including CreativeUp, a Santa Barbara-based company that formed at one of his earliest events and is still operating more than six years later.
Jacques Chirazi , Director of the Basement and Entrepreneurship Center at UC San Diego's Office of Innovation and Commercialization, brings UC San Diego's student entrepreneurship ecosystem into the weekend, connecting participants to campus resources that can carry momentum well past Sunday night.
Mason Baldwin : TBD
This isn't just a competition — it's an entrepreneurial laboratory. Participants who've never attempted a startup get to try on different roles — founder, designer, engineer — and learn by doing what Julian calls "experiential education entrepreneurship," packed into three days.

About Event

Hosted by DNAForge
One focused day for biology students, early-career scientists, and technical builders to turn consequential biological problems into working prototypes.
Saturday, November 14th, 2026
Hours: 9:00 AM–9:00 PM
Scale: About 100 participants
Three tracks
Three domains where biological judgment and technical execution must meet. Choose a problem worth a day of concentrated work.
Therapeutics. Build tools that help researchers design, evaluate, or deliver new treatments.

Biosecurity. Build practical defenses for biological risks, laboratory safety, and preparedness.

Agricultural resilience. Build for healthier crops, stronger food systems, and biological climate adaptation.

Who belongs in the room
Biological fluency is a building skill. Early-career scientists, wet-lab researchers, computational biologists, clinicians, agricultural scientists, ML researchers, software engineers, and designers.
Application principles
Applications are individual. If you want to attend with a team, every person on that team must submit their own application. Listing teammates in your application does not apply for them.

Teams can form before or during the event. We will help admitted participants find complementary collaborators.

Applying does not guarantee admission. DNAForge reviews each application for this limited-capacity event.

The event is in person. Every applicant must confirm they can attend in Berkeley for the full participant program.

Admissions timeline
Apply early. Every applicant gets a clear status.
October 25th: Priority deadline. Applications received by this date receive first consideration.

October 28th: First decisions. The first admission decisions are planned for this date.

November 6th: Final cutoff. Last day to submit an individual application.

November 7th: Final waitlist decisions. Remaining applicants receive their planned final status.

MTC Berkeley , Modal , Boltz , Tamarind Bio , GXL , Carbon Fellowship , and BenchFlow .

About Event

Who Killed the Build? 💀
A Halloween DevTools Murder Mystery with Flox
The build is dead. The cause? Unknown.
Join AI Valley and Flox for a Halloween devtools night where you’ll investigate what went wrong, follow the clues, and figure out who (or what) killed the build.
Instead of a traditional product demo, Flox will take us through an interactive investigation of a broken development environment. Along the way, you’ll uncover suspicious dependencies, environment issues, and other clues before making your final guess.
🔎 Investigate the crime scene
💻 See Flox in action
🕵️ Follow the clues and solve the mystery
🎃 Enjoy Halloween food, drinks, and networking
Costumes are encouraged. Production incidents are not.
Meet the Speakers

Justin Castilla — Flox

Jessica Garson Beauchemin — Runpod

Amin Karbas — Resolve AI

Dan Gross — FriendliAI

Agenda
5:00–6:00 PM — Doors Open + Halloween Food, Drinks & Networking
6:00–6:10 PM — The Crime Scene: Welcome from AI Valley + Flox and meet the speakers
6:10–7:00 PM — The Investigation: Talks and demos with Justin Castilla (Flox), Jessica Garson Beauchemin (Runpod), Amin Karbas (Resolve AI), and Dan Gross (FriendliAI), with clues revealed throughout
7:00–8:00 PM — Halloween Mixer + Food, Drinks & Networking
About HAC
Hanwha AI Center (HAC) is a private membership for all those dedicated to AI. As a hub for innovation, HAC brings together passionate entrepreneurs, researchers, and visionaries to explore the societal and technological impacts of AI on human life.
Flox is a developer tool that creates reproducible, hash-pinned software environments across laptops, CI pipelines, and production. It eliminates environment drift by using a single configuration file to lock exact software versions everywhere. Flox is powered by the Nix package manager, but simplifies the experience so users do not have to write Nix code directly.
AI Valley is a community rooted in supporting exceptional first generation builders, founders, and creators. We curate environments where ambitious people meet collaborators, mentors, and opportunities through hackathons, workshops, and intimate gatherings across AI, tech, and the arts. Join Qualcomm and HackerSquad for an evening of hands-on building with Arduino UNO Q , a platform that combines real-time microcontroller control, Linux-class computing, and edge AI capabilities in a single board. About Event

Car AI Navigation Hackathon

Challenge: We have a mini city road with lanes, intersection and traffic signs. Your job is to use AI and a small autonomous car like the Donkeycar or equivalent (typically 1/16th scale or smaller RC car with a Raspberry Pi or equivalent and a camera controlling it) to navigate the "city", obeying signs and making it from one side to the other in the fastest time.

You must bring your own car, which should be ready to run, with compute and camera already onboard and working. The objective of the hackathon is to add AI "city" navigation to it.

You can use onboard AI, AI on your laptop via Wifi or AI in the cloud to help with the navigation. Think creatively about what kind of AI to use and what's the fastest way to do it!

This is not an event for spectators, nor will cars be provided to those who arrive without one. This is a hackathon, not a regular race. Come ready to hack!

About Event

Learn how to deploy and optimize AI workloads on Arm from cloud to edge through technical sessions, demos, and interactive experiences.
Explore Gemma optimization, Google AI Edge and LiteRT, PyTorch and ExecuTorch, power-aware profiling, agentic AI, and physical AI. Hear from experts at Arm, Google DeepMind, Google, Renesas, and Nota AI.
What to expect
💻 Explore cloud-to-edge AI workflows
Explore AI technologies and workflows spanning cloud to edge, with technical sessions and demos from Arm engineers and ecosystem experts.
⚡ Try interactive AI demos and challenges
Explore agentic and physical AI through interactive demos, and test your skills with developer challenges throughout the day.
🪪 Hack your Arm-powered digital badge
Get your own Arm-powered digital badge to personalize and hack during the event.
🤝 Connect with engineers and developers
Ask questions and connect directly with Arm engineers, ecosystem partners, and other developers.
